study type: Population-based cohort study (record linkage study with nested sibling comparison)
outcome: grade achieved on leaving secondary education
cohort: The study included 2,008,102 Swedish children born between 1973 and 1994, with a nested comparison of 439,629 siblings.
finding: Pre- and post-term children, as well as those born small-for-gestational age, exhibited lower average grades in secondary education compared to full-term counterparts, suggesting independent effects of fetal maturation and fetal growth on school performance.
followup_time: Until leaving secondary education (late adolescence/early adulthood)
birth_weight: Categorized by weight-for-gestational age, including small-for-gestational age
gest_age: Ranging from extremely pre-term (24 completed weeks) to extremely post-term (45 completed weeks), including pre-term, post-term, and full-term categories
